title: In 2005, scientists germinated a date palm seed recovered decades earlier from the ruins of Masada,
description:
In 2005, scientists germinated a date palm seed recovered decades earlier from the ruins of Masada, Israel, one of the oldest seeds ever known to sprout. The seed had been sitting in storage since the original excavation in the 1960s.

planted the ancient seed and coaxed it into germinating, then watched it grow into a healthy young date palm they named Methuselah.

roughly the age of the seed that grew into Methuselah, and roughly how long it had been since a tree from this ancient line last bore fruit.

Methuselah turned out to be male, so it could produce pollen but never fruit on its own. Researchers later germinated more ancient seeds from other sites, and some grew into female trees. Growing a 2,000-year-old seed at all was the hard part. Getting an actual harvest still took another cross of trees.

One of those female trees, named Hannah, was hand-pollinated using Methuselah's pollen. By the early 2020s the cross had produced real dates grown from an ancient Judean seed line, something nobody had eaten in two thousand years.

Sources:
- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Judean_date_palm: covers the approximately 2,000-year-old date palm seeds recovered from archaeological excavations at Masada, Israel, in the 1960s, the germination of one seed in 2005 by Dr Sarah Sallon and Dr Elaine Solowey, its naming as Methuselah, its growth into a male, pollen-producing tree, the later germination of several female seeds from other ancient sites, and successful hand-pollination between Methuselah and a female tree named Hannah leading to the first dates grown from ancient seeds in roughly 2,000 years.
